📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The uproar over the alleged use of generative AI imagery in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” has taken a familiar path. Early responses to the Netflix film penned by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher have pointed out egregious examples of generative video artifacts sticking out in key flashback moments in the film — including one shot from the trailer where it certainly looks like a video AI program rendered a wagon the wrong way around.

Recent findings suggest that the criticism is of the use of generative AI in principle as a fundamental betrayal of the creative process — but it’s also of Fincher, as a director who, historically, has been meticulous with the level of detail and intention in every single shot of his films. In the early responses to Fincher’s latest, there’s been a lot of surprise and disappointment about this particular filmmaker being caught up in an AI controversy. Related Stories Trump Renews Backing for Federal Film Tax Credit as Lawmakers Push for Year-End Passage ‘Disclosure Day’ Did Its Biggest Stunts Practically, So the VFX Team Worked Hard to Look Invisible — Watch.

Recent findings suggest that at first blush, his approach seems at odds with using generative AI video, which relies on regurgitated (and, it bears repeating every time, stolen) data. But Fincher has defended his use of AI to the LA Times as a way to continue to innovate on an art form that is, after all, just over a hundred years old.

Sources indicate that that defense really shouldn’t be surprising, given Fincher’s history with AI specifically. Although he’s been critical of generative tools in the past, Fincher admitted to using them (never publicly disclosing which) in the 4K remaster of “Se7en,” which the director described as a process of needing to remake the negative in order to battle the ravages of time (and the thousands of tiny scratches that would show up in 4K). “If you could see a 30-year-old negative and what it looks like even when immaculately stored — it was an enormous amount of fixing, just digs and scratches and cinch,” he told EW at the time.

That kind of image restoration technology was around long, long before the Anthropic IPO failed to save the stock market, but its level of precision has increased enormously in the past year. There were also sequences in the stored “Se7en,” though, where generative tech filled in gaps from the original. For one example, Fincher talked about a moment where a camera pan overshot the mark and changedh a shot. The performance had been good enough to use a technically flawed take — and, combined wit an unused take, allowed software to generate the missing information and restore the intended image.

“It ends up being the most thrillingly stupid fix in the world because if you see it, we didn’t do our jobs. And you probably won’t see it. You probably won’t be aware that it’s happened. But you look at it, and you just think to yourself, ‘It’s so nice that we can fix that kind of stuff today,'” Fincher told Collider about that moment in “Se7en.”.

By Fincher’s own lights, then, the problem with AI in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is that people are painfully aware of it. AI critics might make a distinction between video restoration tools that work on existing projects and those tools being used because they can more quickly and cheaply generate originals that would’ve otherwise needed to be crafted by human hands. Having something AI-generated isn’t necessarily better than nothing when it comes to art, and choosing to AI-generate a Western chase sequence inside of, say, 10 seconds isn’t a solution to all.

In a recent development, still, Fincher knows what he’s doing. This past week, he emphasized to the LA Times that he’s not a Luddite when it comes to film: “We’re talking about a thing that’s a hundred years old, and everyone’s going, ‘Stop. Pencils down. No more iterating. It’s not necessary to have at your fingertips the ability to change the color of that person’s eyes.’ Well, it exists. Should we not use it?”.

Industry observers note that the answer is an emphatic “No!” to some And they can certainly be mad, or disappointed, or disheartened about Fincher’s decision to use AI tools. The one thing they shouldn’t be is surprised.

It has been revealed that william Gibson is one of the most influential authors in the sci-fi genre. Often credited for pioneering the cyberpunk subgenre, his most seminal novel, Neuromancer, remains a sci-fi masterpiece in 2026. Despite the timelessness and popularity of his literary work, however, his cyberpunk stories and books have hardly been adapted for the screen.

Recent findings suggest that while many video games, movies, and TV reveals have loosely drawn from his work, there are only a handful of direct mainstream adaptations of his stories. Two of these, Johnny Mnemonic and Latest Rose Hotel, premiered in the '90s and struggled to leave their mark. One, titled The Peripheral, premiered on Prime Video in 2022 before being canceled after one season.

Sources indicate that considering the long-standing legacy and influence of William Gibson's work, it is unfortunate that none of his adaptations have worked too well on the screen so far. However, this will soon likely change. Apple TV is now adapting one of William Gibson's most iconic cyberpunk sci-fi books, Neuromancer, which has the potential to become one of the biggest events of the genre in this decade.

It has been revealed that most cyberpunk TV shows and movies focus a little too much on the visual aspect, featuring neon-soaked cityscapes and edgy characters. Prime Video's The Peripheral, on the other hand, truly understood the essence of William Gibson's near-future cyberpunk. In its 2032 timeline, the show features a very familiar, economically broken rural America.

Technology is deeply grafted onto the blue-collar lives of regular people. There are 3-D printed pharmaceuticals, while even veterans with disabilities use military implants called "haptics." The series also reveals its central VR technology as a form of escapism for the main characters who place it in a run-down trailer.

Then comes the show's 2099 timeline where it contrasts 2032's "low lives" with London's high-tech and elite. This is when The Peripheral also introduces "The Jackpot," to reveal the high stakes of its apocalyptic conflict and how humanity's unchecked ambition in the future has pushed civilization to the brink of collapse.

In its 8-episode runtime, Prime Video's The Peripheral did enough to earn more follow-ups and expand its sci-fi vision in season 2. It was a rare adaptation that embraced the hard-edged sci-fi and weirdness of its source material. Unfortunately, despite being promising, its renewal was reversed by Prime Video after SAG-AFTRA and Writers Guild of America's strikes in 2023.

Recent findings suggest that the works of many sci-fi authors, like Philip K. Dick, are not easy to adapt. Yet, Philip K. Dick's stories have already received multiple worthy on-screen adaptations. William Gibson's adaptations, in contrast, have almost been cursed. The ones like Johnny Mnemonic became cult classics, but never achieved mainstream acclaim or success.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, The Peripheral had immense potential, but failed to last beyond one season. After being considered "unfilmable" for quite some time, William Gibson's Neuromancer is finally being adapted by Apple TV. And so far, it looks like the show will finally spell redemption for William Gibson's adaptations.

It has been revealed that apple TV's history of bringing challenging adaptations like Isaac Asimov's Foundation to the screen alone is a proof of concept for its ability to successfully translate "unfilmable" sci-fi literature. William Gibson, too, has been directly involved with the show's production, which also heavily favors the adaptation.

It has been revealed that not to mention, after its first trailer, it looks like Apple TV's Neuromancer is not bogging down William Gibson's original vision. If all goes well, the upcoming sci-fi series could become a massive hit and make up for the pitfalls and cancelation of Prime Video's The Peripheral.

Coupled COMSOL models of electromagnetic propagation, microwave absorption, heat transfer, and ceramic sintering kinetics are used to predict temperature evolution, reaction progression, spatial resolution, and processing scalability. Future extensions will incorporate pulsed excitation, fluid flow, resin viscosity, convection, shrinkage, and solid mechanics.Together, these examples demonstrate how the COMSOL software can integrate multiphysics modeling with sensing, manufacturing, and data inversion. Tom Hanks is no stranger to a family-favorite movie. Earlier this year, he starred again in one of the best family franchises of all timeas Toy Story 5 and a fight against modern technology was unleashed on global audiences. Woody, Buzz (Tim Allen), Jessie (Joan Cusack), and the rest of the toys returned to huge success, scoring more than $1 billion at the global box office, which right now ranks as the year's third-highest-grossing film.

Sources indicate that unlike Toy Story 4, this fifth installment was also a big hit with critics. "The impressive fifth installment not only justifies its existence but feels like a necessary response to how much the world has changed in the past three decades," wrote Collider's Taylor Gates, who gave the movie an 8/10 rating in her review. Hanks is a go-to voice for a family animated movie to succeed, something that happened when he joined the cast of his only feature-length Christmas film to date, voicing an impressive five characters.

Industry observers note that the Polar Express, directed by Hanks' long-time collaborator Robert Zemeckis, was released in 2004 and has since become a festive favorite in households across the globe. However, reviewers were mixed in their initial response, criticizing the film's supposed uncanny animation, which has now been reframed as part of the film's quirky charm. The Polar Express earned $320 million at the global box office, split between a domestic haul of $196 million and a further $124 million from overseas markets, and against a reported $170 million. 22 years later, the film is a hit again as the festive season begins. At the time of writing, The Polar Express is one of the ten most-watched movies on HBO Max and has surpassed the 100-day mark on the streamer.

As The Polar Express scores big on streaming, Hanks fans can look forward to one of his most beloved '90s movies officially getting the reboot treatment. Earlier this month, Warner Bros. confirmed it was bringing back Hanks' 1998 rom-com favorite, You've Got Mail, with Jason Orley attached to direct. Orley is working on a script that is based on a previous take by Deborah Kaplan and Harry Elfont, with most other details being kept tightly under wraps.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Professional and amateur photographers just got a new alternative for editing and managing their photos on Mac with the release of VSCO Studio Pro, a native macOS app that brings the company’s popular editing tools to the desktop for the first time.
  • More than that, VSCO Studio Pro integrates with the firm’s broader ecosystem of photography tools, allowing consumers to manage their workflow from importing and editing photos to delivering finished images to clients through VSCO Galleries, without having to manually export and upload them to another app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the company’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside newly introduced features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details.

Professional and amateur photographers just got a new alternative for editing and managing their photos on Mac with the release of VSCO Studio Pro, a native macOS app that brings the company’s popular editing tools to the desktop for the first time.

More than that, VSCO Studio Pro integrates with the firm’s broader ecosystem of photography tools, allowing consumers to manage their workflow from importing and editing photos to delivering finished images to clients through VSCO Galleries, without having to manually export and upload them to another app.

It also supports keyboard shortcuts similar to those found in other popular photo editors, making it easier for photographers familiar with those apps to get started.

Here’s Eric Wittman, CEO of VSCO, on today’s launch:.

“Photographers deserve tools built around how they actually work. […] 75% of VSCO Pro members have used our presets in the last six months. Now those looks live on the desktop, with one connected workflow from camera to client delivery and nothing getting in the way.

According to recent reports, the first thing users will notice, and then continue to notice when using VSCO Studio Pro, is how fast it is. From changing the grid size, to sorting images, to applying presets by rolling the cursor over each of the 200+ presets, pretty much everything about VSCO Studio Pro feels as real-time and instant as it can be when dealing with large numbers of images.

Sources indicate that as for importing photos, VSCO Studio Pro supports Apple Photos, local folders, SD cards, and external drives, and offers RAW compatibility with more than 800 cameras from 20 brands. Users can also choose whether to work with files in their original location or copy them elsewhere.

Under the hood, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop combines Apple’s Core Image RAW processing with the organization’s own Reflex image processing engine, which handles presets and editing adjustments.

Batch editing in VSCO Studio Pro Desktop can handle anywhere from two to 500 images at once, which is great for swiftly applying the same preset or film-inspired look (including Kodak Portra, Kodachrome, Fujifilm Velvia, and Kodak Tri-X), or making adjustments to an entire set of photos simultaneously, with changes appearing across all selected images in real time.

It has been revealed that and speaking of presets, VSCO Studio Pro packs an exclusive one called IOE1 Pro, developed with photographer Joe Greer. IOE1 Pro, as well as VSCO’s other presets, allow people to adjust the strength, color, tone, and contrast, further helping them fine-tune each look to their liking.

VSCO Studio Pro’s editing tools include the usual suspects photographers might expect from photo editing software, including exposure, contrast, fade, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, skin tone, temperature, tint, hue, saturation, lightness, sharpening, clarity, vignetting, and grain adjustments for strength, size, and color.

VSCO is also working to expand its toolset to include bloom and halation effects, curves, masks, and a remove tool for users looking for more control over their edits and to make more precise, localized adjustments to their images.

Also in the works are fresh organizational features, including projects for managing groups of photos, as well as culling tools that will allow consumers to rate images with stars and mark them as accepted or rejected, making it easier to sort through large photo collections.

Sources indicate that once consumers are happy with their adjustments, they can export their photos individually or in batches, choosing the file name, format, resolution, and compression quality. VSCO Studio Pro also offers resizing presets for web, social media, and client delivery, as well as the option to save the finished images to a folder of their choice.

And speaking of client delivery, owners can publish their edited photos directly to VSCO Galleries, allowing them to share full-resolution images without having to export them and upload them separately elsewhere.

In a recent development, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop is available today as a free download for Apple Silicon Macs, with full feature access requiring a VSCO Pro membership, starting at $4.99 per month or $59.99 per year, or a VSCO One membership. You can see it in action below:.

To learn more about VSCO Studio Pro Desktop, follow this link.

Tom Hardy's 142-Minute Near-Perfect Miniseries Still Has Not Been Beaten

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Two things can be true at once with Tom Hardy: he vanishes into roles with all the finesse of a deep-cover spy, and we never forget who we're watching.
  • It has been revealed that in 2009, right before Hardy vaulted into household name status, he left his mark on one of classic literature's most infamous, analyzed, and misrepresented figures.
  • Recent findings suggest that and while Brontë's descriptions of Heathcliff contain a degree of racial ambiguity, she inarguably establishes him as a man of color — an imperative fact that the majority of filmmakers have neglected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two things can be true at once with Tom Hardy: he vanishes into roles with all the finesse of a deep-cover spy, and we never forget who we're watching. Such awareness isn't a negative, though; when Hardy signs his name to a project, said story arrives at our doorsteps with the rubber-stamped guarantee that he has wholeheartedly thrown himself into the character. The palpably realistic and sometimes avant-garde mannerisms, voice shifts, and physical transformations seem effortless, but audiences know the road to Hardy's results is all dedicated effort.

It has been revealed that in 2009, right before Hardy vaulted into household name status, he left his mark on one of classic literature's most infamous, analyzed, and misrepresented figures. Emily Brontë simultaneously refined and created an archetype with Wuthering Heights, and countless riffs on Heathcliff — equal parts brooding antagonist and tragic antihero — have followed in her landmark footsteps since 1847. Every time a newly introduced movie or television adaptation rolls around, actors covet the ingeniously rich part. Many have delivered fine performances, but only a handful have gotten close enough to graze their fingertips against Wuthering Heights' stormy and tormented soul.

Recent findings suggest that and while Brontë's descriptions of Heathcliff contain a degree of racial ambiguity, she inarguably establishes him as a man of color — an imperative fact that the majority of filmmakers have neglected. Without ever diminishing or excusing such consistent whitewashing, Hardy's take on Healthcliff is also one of the most definitive interpretations by far. The two-part miniseries itself remains the adaptational gold standard to date, too — desolate, macabre, bitter, thematically accurate, and feverishly intoxicating.

Wuthering Heights is a magnificently tricky puzzle to crack on the page and even more difficult to translate onto the screen. Rather than the straightforward doomed love story it has often been mistaken for, Brontë's morbid and profoundly thoughtful work uncompromisingly interrogates class hierarchy, generational trauma, domestic and systemic abuse cycles, gender and race, obsessive grief, all-consuming revenge, and psychosexual subtext.

Four love stories, four completely different ideas of what it means to be somebody's person. This is the one that matches how you actually fall, and what it would ask of you.

In a recent development, you do not fall for strangers. You fall for the person you have already been talking to for years, which is the slowest and by some distance the most durable way anybody has found to do this.

Recent findings suggest that you want a partner, not an audience. Somebody who wants their own life as badly as you want yours, and who would never ask you to be smaller to make the relationship easier.

The intensity was never the problem. The secrecy is. You are drawn to a love that lives entirely in private, and to the particular ache of wanting somebody you are not supposed to want.

In a recent development, you do not do this cautiously. When it happens for you it is immediate and total and it rearranges everything, and you would not accept a smaller version of it.

According to recent reports, the 2009 limited series does justice to her vast scope, truncates little, and softens nothing. Writer Peter Bowker achieves maximum faithfulness, preserving the thematic integrity in general and by including the crucial plot beats other adaptations abandon for the sake of streamlined simplicity; eliminating the second generation of children negates Brontë's prevailing points. Bowker's scripts employ a flashback structure instead of a traditional chronological approach, which prevents the second episode from losing momentum and gives both halves equal weight.

Sources indicate that coky Giedroyc's direction might not contain the same level of moody lavishness as a high-budget Hollywood affair, but for 2009-era network television, the atmosphere is precisely on point. By day, the visuals luxuriate in the windswept and rocky Yorkshire Moors like the terrain is a private paradise; by night, those same locations drip with an ominous, rain-soaked, Gothic chill no warm coat or feeble lantern light can protect against. If anything, the production's subtle efficiency enables the performers to sell the emotional turbulence with maximum artistic freedom and commitment.

In a way, Heathcliff is a perfect example of Hardy both playing against type and tapping into his exact strengths. It's a demanding role, and he unearths the complete spectrum — every paradoxical layer of aching loneliness, tender desperation, wounded pride, extreme intelligence, seething spite, and punitive cruelty. A defiant survivor of abuse, ostracization, and rejection, he's understated and internalized at one moment, his eyes hollowed out by the phantoms of regret, before gliding straight into visceral rage. He can invade and dominate a room through the sheer force of his insidious physicality, yet still exert a seductively appealing gravitational pull.

Sources indicate that and a Heathcliff, of course, is nothing without his beloved Cathy Earnshaw (Charlotte Riley). Another exceedingly intricate and tricky role, Riley makes Cathy as irresistible, isolated, selfish, jealous, and demanding as she should be. The woman's whims are as untethered as the wind and as dangerous as a sparking live wire; she relishes exerting control by playfully toying with her lovers. In tandem, Riley sells the overwhelming sincerity of Cathy's volatile emotions; it's readily apparent and tragic why her gilded-cage aristocratic life kills her unsatiated spirit long before it kills her body. The war between her contradictory desires — liberated freedom versus conforming to society's standards for financial security and comfort — plays across her face like an Expressionist painting.

Industry observers note that hardy and Riley's chemistry is so naturally thunderous that the pair married five years after filming Wuthering Heights. They capture the characters' star-crossed toxicity in all its smothering closeness, from two young and powerless outcasts who forge a home together and consume each other's chaotic passion like oxygen, to venomous snakes inflicting reciprocal misery until both parties self-destruct. Cathy and Heathcliff is no great love story by any aspirational or enviable measure. However, as terrible, damaged, and lost people who recognize their twin flame, but ruin the solace for which they yearn, they're perfect for each other — as near-perfect as this masterpiece adaptation.

With tasks, Google’s “goal is for Gemini to save you time and money.” Google shared use cases like:.

With today’s announcement, Google is emphasizing that “Gemini is your best choice as a personal assistant because [your emails, calendar, passwords, photos, files, and payment cards] already lives at Google securely, and you don’t have to send it elsewhere.”.

Behind the scenes, Gemini tasks work in your own “hardware-isolated virtual machine” that’s sandboxed and has protections against prompt injection, while leveraging Google Safe Browsing when browsing the web.

Other safety features include having you confirm purchases and asking “clarifying questions if an instruction is ambiguous.”.

Powered by the upcoming Hydrogen model, free Gemini tasks are available in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India.

#85658. Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1156 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • According to recent reports, GTA 6 is absurdly large.
  • It has been revealed that alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most important tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

It has been revealed that alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Industry observers note that let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

It has been revealed that file size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

It has been revealed that according to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

First, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

It has been revealed that if you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

Recent findings suggest that more importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

It has been revealed that the DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

Sources indicate that the Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

Recent findings suggest that if you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for newly introduced hardware, this might be your best bet.

Xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

Save $100 on this excellent gaming headset from Razer, with haptic feedback, a handy base station, and multiple connectivity options.

Make no mistake, this headset is aiming for the top end of gaming peripherals with its MSRP, but it might just achieve it.

It’s comfortable, with an aluminum frame that’s durable but relatively light at 397g, connectivity via Razer’s HyperSpeed Wireless dongle, Bluetooth, wired USB, or a 3.5mm jack, and even simultaneous 2.4GHz and Bluetooth audio, so you can listen to a podcast on your phone while playing a game that doesn’t require as much brainpower.

The handy retractable mic uses Razer’s TriForce Driver design for a wider soundstage that’s free of distortion, and THX Spatial Audio brings everything together.

Still, those are somewhat “meat and potatoes” inclusions for any headset worth its salt: So what’s really the draw here? Industry observers note that there’s also a handy OLED base station where you can adjust your listening mode, audio EQ, haptics, lighting, and just about anything else. And you can get up to 50 hours of battery life on a single charge: ideal for a WoW Forever marathon (or two).

#85654. 5 Essential Classic Books for Beginners

5 Essential Classic Books for Beginners

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that at any given moment, Scott Simone has at least three books jockeying for his attention.
  • He’s spent so much time in book shops over the years he is, to his wife’s chagrin, continuing to build a library that doesn’t quite respect the dimensions of the apartment meant to contain it.
  • Sources indicate that if you don't want someone to read a book, tell them it’s a classic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that at any given moment, Scott Simone has at least three books jockeying for his attention. He’ll never turn down a campus novel with a literary bent, nor will he hesitate to add yet another mystery to his Leaning Tower of Pisa-inspired to-be-read pile — which is built upon the bedrocks of too many short story collections, how-are-these-real true crime books, and classics waiting to be cracked open again. Topics that have him ripping through pages the fastest include closed-circle murders, unhappy professors, life-questioning philosophical deep dives, so long as they feature sharp sentences, a dark sense of humor, and at least a little malice.

He’s spent so much time in book shops over the years he is, to his wife’s chagrin, continuing to build a library that doesn’t quite respect the dimensions of the apartment meant to contain it.

Sources indicate that if you don't want someone to read a book, tell them it’s a classic. Tell them that it changed literature. Tell them how generations of writers have tried and failed to reproduce it. Tell them no bookshelf is complete without it. Now you’ve made reading a chore. It’s homework. We seem more interested in what these books represent than what's actually between their covers. But none of that tells you whether you'll enjoy spending an afternoon with one.

And God help you if you don't enjoy one. Give up on a modern novel halfway through, and it's simply not for you. Put down a classic, and feel the judgment pour. Somebody will come along to explain what you did wrong. Perhaps you didn't understand the historical context. Maybe you missed the symbolism. Give it another go in 10 years, when you're older and a little wiser. Sometimes that's fair. But we've developed a habit of treating difficulty as a mark of greatness, as though the more you struggle through a book, the more worthwhile the experience. And that's a shame. These were novels — funny, exciting, full of people behaving appallingly — long before they became monuments to literature. And perhaps the best way to appreciate their greatness is to remember what made them worth reading in the first place.

If you think 19th-century literature is a slog, Jane Austen would like a word. And in all likelihood, it'll be a funny one. Because Austen knows how to bring the humor, especially when she's eviscerating the types of people who tend to make fools of themselves. Pride and Prejudice rotates a cast of such characters right into her firing line. There's Mrs. Bennet, who's basically willing to marry off her five daughters to whichever eligible bachelors wander into the neighborhood. There's Mr. Collins, a man so impressed with himself he has no doubt everyone else must be, too. And then there's Elizabeth Bennet, who's clever enough to recognize everyone else's shortcomings, but isn't quite so perceptive when it comes to her own. The best part: You don't need to know much about Regency England to appreciate any of this. Snobs, bores, and people who think far too highly of themselves were plentiful two centuries ago, and Austen brings them hilariously to life.

Sources indicate that the romance is familiar enough, too. Elizabeth and the wealthy-but-insufferable Mr. Darcy spend an awful lot of time misunderstanding one another, taking offense at perfectly innocent remarks, and refusing to admit when they've been wrong. It's not so far removed from a modern romantic comedy, though there's more at stake than a few bruised egos. Money and social standing dictate much of what these people can and can't do, especially when it comes to marriage. For Elizabeth and her sisters, finding a suitable husband is as much a matter of financial security as it is romance. Yes, the language does take some getting used to, and polite society and all its rules can seem ridiculous. But Austen thought plenty of them were ridiculous, too, and she's more than happy to have a little fun at their expense.

Industry observers note that not every literary classic takes a fortnight to actually get going. Case in point: Around the World in Eighty Days. Jules Verne takes a simple premise, launches out of the gates with it, and never really slows his pace. Which can't exactly be noted for Phileas Fogg, an English gentleman who seems a little too obsessed with punctuality. Yet he wagers £20,000 that he can travel around the globe in 80 days. This being 1872 and all, a time when travel involved nothing more than a few steamships and trains, it's an outrageous proposition. But that's all the setup Verne needs. There's no sprawling cast to keep track of and no complicated backstory to untangle. There's simply a man and a deadline — and a ridiculous number of obstacles standing between the two.

Fogg, mind you, is hardly the sort of man you'd expect to go gallivanting around the world. He's a creature of habit, so wedded to his daily routine that you'd think the slightest disruption would send him into a fit. However, Verne seems determined to test just how much the man can take. A train is missed. A connection falls through. An itinerary becomes useless. Somehow, Fogg takes it all in stride, with the composure of a man who's been told his dinner reservation has been pushed back 15 minutes. His French valet, Passepartout, isn't so accommodating, and watching him fret while his employer barely bats an eye is half the fun. And Verne makes us fret along with him. A delayed departure becomes genuinely suspenseful. Some of the novel's attitudes toward the people and places encountered along the way are decidedly of their time; but Verne's talent for turning a simple journey into one calamity after another hasn't aged much at all.

Not every difficult subject makes for a difficult book. Leo Tolstoy takes on death and regret. He delves into the despair of a life wasted in The Death of Ivan Ilyich, and he manages it in about 100 pages. The writing is surprisingly straightforward, the cast is small, and there's hardly any plot to untangle. We learn that Ivan, a Russian judge, has died before we've even had a chance to meet the man. So there's no great mystery about where this is headed. What concerns Tolstoy is how Ivan got there, and why a man who's done just about everything expected of him finds himself so unprepared for the end. It's heavy stuff, sure. But you don't need a philosophy degree or much knowledge of 19th-century Russia to understand what Tolstoy's getting at.

It has been revealed that tolstoy has a wicked sense of humor, which helps. Ivan's colleagues hear that he's died and immediately start calculating what it might mean for their careers. His funeral is treated as an inconvenience, something to get through before going about life. Ivan himself hasn't exactly spent his years pursuing a life of great meaning. He's been too busy climbing the social ladder and worrying about what people might think of him. Then he gets sick, and suddenly none of it seems worth much. Worse still, the people around him would sooner carry on pretending everything is fine than acknowledge what's happening to him. Tolstoy has plenty of fun exposing all this vanity and self-importance.

Recent findings suggest that toni Collette and Kit Harington are shooting a new Miss Marple and 20th Century has several more Christies in development, so the drawing room is busier than it has been in decades. Here is which of them you are, and the case for yours being the best.

Recent findings suggest that order, method, and a quiet confidence that you are the cleverest person present. Poirot is a retired Belgian police officer who solves murders by sitting still and thinking, and who is vain enough to make the reveal a performance every single time.

People tell you things because they cannot imagine you being a threat. Marple solves murders by comparing everybody to somebody she once knew in St Mary Mead, which sounds like a joke until you notice it works every time, because human beings are not as original as they think.

Sources indicate that you have far too many ideas and roughly a fifth of them are excellent. Ariadne Oliver is a successful crime novelist who is sick of her famous foreign detective and keeps saying so, which is Christie writing about Christie and getting away with it completely.

You are steady, decent and the reason the difficult genius has anybody at all. Hastings narrates the early Poirot novels, misses most of the clues, and is the only character in the books that Poirot is unambiguously fond of, which tells you what he is really for.

Industry observers note that you can spend eons trying to decipher Franz Kafka. Literary scholars have been at it for more than a century. But The Metamorphosis doesn't require much deciphering to enjoy. Kafka gives us the whole ridiculous premise in his opening sentence: Gregor Samsa, a traveling salesman, wakes up as an enormous insect. Gregor's reaction is almost as absurd as the transformation itself. He's worried about being late for work. He's missed his train, his boss is going to be furious, and his family needs the money. The man's no longer human, and he's fretting about how he'll explain his absence to his employer. It's horribly funny, especially because the thinking behind it isn't all that difficult to recognize.

Kafka's joke gets considerably darker as the story goes on. Gregor has spent years working to support his parents and sister, putting their needs ahead of his own. Now that he's the one who needs looking after, the family isn't exactly enthusiastic to act in kind. His sister initially takes pity on him. His father can barely stand the sight of him. Eventually, everyone gets a bit sick and tired of having an enormous insect in their house. All the while, Gregor seems more concerned about becoming a burden than he does about his own misery. It's an awful arrangement, but one that doesn't take much imagination to understand.

It has been revealed that nella Larsen proves you don't need a murder or mayhem for a gripping psychological thriller. She managed to do so with an old friendship and a few uncomfortable conversations. Passing is barely 150 pages, but Larsen packs enough suspicion and intrigue to fill hundreds more. It centers on two Black women, Irene Redfield and Clare Kendry, childhood friends who've taken very different paths in life. Clare passes as white, even marrying a wealthy white man who’d never guess she's Black. Odd, considering he's so viciously racist. On the other hand, Irene has built a comfortable life in Harlem, and she knows just how badly Clare's deception could end. But when the two reconnect, she can't bring herself to stay away.

In a recent development, there's plenty to worry about, but it's the conversations between Irene and Clare that make the novel so fraught. Larsen lets Irene do much of the interpreting for us, and we fall into the habit of taking her word for it. Clare is reckless. Clare craves attention. Clare is putting everyone at risk. And perhaps she's right about all of it. But the more we learn about Irene, the harder it becomes to separate genuine concern from jealousy and resentment. Larsen is great at making us suspicious of someone without giving us much evidence against them. So much so that an ordinary conversation can seem loaded with meaning, a perfectly innocent remark like a veiled threat. And so we find ourselves scrutinizing every little exchange, wondering who's being truthful and who's got something to hide.

Recent findings suggest that xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink promptly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

Industry observers note that the X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

These upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 launched at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also important to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing new firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

#85646. Anya Taylor-Joy’s Sci-Fi Thriller Is Still Her Greatest Movie 2 Years Later

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (738 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Collider ↗ Open Full Page

Anya Taylor-Joy’s Sci-Fi Thriller Is Still Her Greatest Movie 2 Years Later

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (738 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anya Taylor-Joy has brought so much to her many hits over the years, but her greatest movie is the one where she says the least.
  • Set years before the events of Fury Road, in the radioactive wasteland of post-apocalyptic Australia, the film follows the path of Furiosa from childhood, where she is played by Alyla Browne, to early adulthood, where Taylor-Joy takes over.
  • Recent findings suggest that the movie is the fifth in the Mad Max franchise, but the first not to prominently feature the character of Max Rockatansky (who appears in a cameo played by Jacob Tomuri, Tom Hardy’s stunt double in Fury Road) — though many fans of the 2015 movie argue that Theron’s performance as Furiosa was the most compelling in the film, and that she was the story’s true lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anya Taylor-Joy has brought so much to her many hits over the years, but her greatest movie is the one where she says the least. The 2024 prequel Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga sees her take over the title role from Charlize Theron and portray the early years of the post-apocalyptic warrior who became the highlight of 2015’s Mad Max: Fury Road. With George Miller’s direction and Taylor-Joy’s exceptional on-screen presence, the movie became an instant classic.

Set years before the events of Fury Road, in the radioactive wasteland of post-apocalyptic Australia, the film follows the path of Furiosa from childhood, where she is played by Alyla Browne, to early adulthood, where Taylor-Joy takes over. Stolen from her idyllic sanctuary home and forcibly adopted by warlord Dementus (Chris Hemsworth), she rises up the ranks of the Citadel, ruled by the tyrannical Immortan Joe (Lachy Hulme). She becomes caught in the middle of the rivalry between the two men, and begins using their ambition to exact revenge and work her way to freedom.

Recent findings suggest that the movie is the fifth in the Mad Max franchise, but the first not to prominently feature the character of Max Rockatansky (who appears in a cameo played by Jacob Tomuri, Tom Hardy’s stunt double in Fury Road) — though many fans of the 2015 movie argue that Theron’s performance as Furiosa was the most compelling in the film, and that she was the story’s true lead. This prequel fulfills that potential with a captivating adventure worthy of its lofty predecessors.

Narratively speaking, Furiosa is an expansion of the world that was introduced in Fury Road. The 2015 film indicated us the landscape passing by at 100 miles per hour, in what was essentially one significant, beautiful chase movie. Max’s mission was simple – race to escape the Citadel, and then turn back to reclaim it. Furiosa’s origin story is more complex, divided into chapters and focused more on the characters involved. The torment she endures, and the loss that hardens her, are all essential to the plot, making for a much darker and more thoughtful movie.

Both are classics, but Miller’s approach is different each time. Fury Road is a practically perfect example of an action movie, with choreography and spectacle that has few equals before or since. Furiosa is an epic revenge tragedy, examining the harrowing path one must take to be compelled to overthrow tyranny. Furiosa must endure, waiting for a moment that is far in the distance, while clinging to the things that keep her soul alive. We also see more world-building, as it is revealed how the Citadel, Gas Town, and Bullet Farm interact. It is an immersive experience, different from Fury Road but brilliant in its own way.

Furiosa is a character who has learned to fly under the radar, blend into any setting, and survive at all costs. This means a character who is very careful with her words, resulting in a leading role with around 30 lines of dialogue. You might think this would be a hindrance for a star, but Taylor-Joy makes it a strength. Using everything except words, she conveys a character being molded into her environment, learning to be relentless and endure anything in the name of getting home. That means a performance that is conveyed by expression, movement, and the smallest of gestures. Great actors overcome limitations to tell stories, and the Golden Globe winner rose to the challenge.

According to recent reports, looking back on the film, the actor noted that Miller had a very specific idea of how she should hold her face, meaning she could only use her eyes to convey emotions for large portions of the movie. “As an actor, where your job is to be able to telegraph how you’re feeling with absolutely everything at your disposal," she told GQ. "To suddenly have everything gone other than [your eyes] was quite petrifying.”.

The gamble paid off, however, as she delivered a soulful, determined performance in the middle of a large-scale action thriller. There are few actors with the discipline, presence, and talent to not only take up the mantle of a beloved character, but to make it their own, and that’s exactly what Taylor-Joy does. For all the many hits of her past, and the exciting projects to come, Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga has a special place in her filmography.

Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (842 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it.
  • In a recent development, I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands.
  • Industry observers note that perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you.

In a recent development, I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands. You can use it one-handed, but for me it’s not nearly as comfortable as the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s too wide and too heavy to be used for long.

Industry observers note that perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions. But that would be a pretty significant shift for me, as there are so many situations when I don’t have both hands free.

If you already use two hands with your iPhone regularly—perhaps because you have a Pro Max model—then the Duo’s one-handed experience likely won’t bother you. But the more I used the Duo, the more I found myself missing my iPhone 18 Pro.

The biggest value proposition of a foldable is that it’s a 2-in-1 product, letting you have a standard phone but also a tablet-sized display that fits in your pocket.

Recent findings suggest that I totally get the appeal, and fully expected to love that hybrid design. But after two weeks of trying, I still struggled to find times when I actually wanted to unfold the Duo. And to be clear, that’s a me problem, not an matter with the Duo itself.

I tried a bunch of apps on the inner display, and struggled to find use cases that—for me—made it worthwhile to open the Duo. But based on the feedback I’ve seen from most Duo owners, I’m very much in the minority.

I know lots of people love the Duo for video, but I don’t watch much video on my iPhone. I almost never watch YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram Reels. And for reveals and movies, I stick with my TV screen and an Apple TV 4K.

Multitasking support on iPhone Duo works really well. But when I found myself needing to multitask, I still reached for my iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard attached. A keyboard-free product can’t replace my main computer (nor would I expect it to), and the Duo screen was too small to comfortably work on it.

Last year I bought an iPhone Air and absolutely loved it. Initially, the Air’s less capable camera system didn’t bother me, it was “good enough.”.

Sources indicate that after a few months though, I started missing the Pro camera system more. Then I learned that my wife was pregnant with twins, and I knew I wanted the best possible iPhone cameras to capture their early weeks and months. So I bought an iPhone 18 Pro in September.

In a recent development, I’ve been very impressed by iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera upgrades, and it’s great having a Telephoto lens again too. Since having the best camera system is so crucial for me right now, I knew iPhone Duo couldn’t be my only iPhone.

I initially planned to dual-carry the two models, using iPhone 18 Pro solely as a camera. But over and over I found myself wishing it was my only iPhone.

I returned mine as well. Beautiful device, but functionally not very good.

According to recent reports, is the iPhone Duo camera good enough for most people? Probably so. But for this year at least, with my twins aging rapidly, it’s not quite right for me. If I loved the Duo for other reasons, I would just use both models. But since I didn’t, I’m happy to stick with the iPhone 18 Pro.

In closing, I want to explicitly state that I don’t think the iPhone Duo is a bad product, and this isn’t a “bad review.”.

Industry observers note that the iPhone Duo just isn’t for me. I get the sense, though, that it’s lots of people’s favorite iPhone in years. Apple created its most unique fresh iPhone model since the original, and there’s plenty to love about it. I’m very curious to see how popular foldables become over time compared to slab models, because each clearly offers pros and cons. But for me, at least right now, the iPhone 18 Pro is my model of choice.

What has your iPhone Duo experience been like so far? Love it? Undecided? Let us know in the comments.

AirPods got a variety of upcoming features this fall in iOS 27, several of which are exclusive to AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179). Here’s everything new.

Custom EQ is a feature that some AirPods users thought Apple would never ship, but iOS 27 adds it.

With Custom EQ, Apple now lets you set your own sound profile for AirPods. Per Apple:.

AirPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV shows and movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.

You can change the EQ by going to your AirPods’ settings ⇾ Audio & Routing ⇾ Equalizer ⇾ Custom. From here, you can adjust the sound profile for low, mid, and high frequencies.

Custom EQ is available on AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, AirPods 5, and AirPods 4.

Sources indicate that apple GymKit has been available for years, but only for Apple Watch. It lets you pair and sync workout data with compatible cardio equipment, like treadmills, ellipticals, indoor bikes, and more.

In iOS 27, GymKit expands to support iPhone using AirPods Pro 3’s heart rate sensor. My colleague Zac gave it a try:.

The setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

In a recent development, once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

For more details on iOS 27’s GymKit feature for AirPods Pro 3, check out Zac’s full hands-on below.

Siri AI is available on compatible iPhone hardware in iOS 27, and Apple made sure to expand full support for the AI assistant to AirPods too.

AirPods are essentially becoming an AI wearable thanks to the new Siri. It will let people do a lot more than the current Siri. Here are some key features via Apple’s website:.

According to recent reports, earlier this year when AirTag 2 launched, Apple brought Precision Finding support to Apple Watch for the first time. Until now though, it’s been limited to AirTag 2.

But with iOS 27 and watchOS 27, Apple expands Precision Finding on the Watch to AirPods Pro 3.

AirPods Pro 3’s case includes the latest second-generation Ultra Wideband (UWB) chip, letting you find it with greater precision and step-by-step guidance right from your wrist.

With every batch of new AirPods features that debuts, the AirPods settings screen in the Settings app gets more cluttered.

But in iOS 27, Apple has a welcome fix: it’s redesigned and reorganized all AirPods settings.

In a recent development, now, you’ll find AirPods settings organized into more categories and submenus, accompanied by colorful icons. It makes finding the right setting way easier and more intuitive than before.
